title: Event log and debugging
goal: Diagnose a defect using safe logs, a debugger and a reproducible scenario.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: Useful logs contain time, case/runID, operation and safe outcome. “Error” alone does not identify the stage or affected document. Use synthetic keys and no secrets. Correlation links request, handler and rejection without dumping a database publicly.

Use an own 30-minute document and reproduce a direct 1441 rejection from module 5. Retain source, actual reference and expected 30 after failure. Exclude real customers, tokens, account contents and license identifiers from the protocol.

Break at the expected branch, inspect types/values and step through. Editing variables is not evidence that the code is correct. Success after manual value injection is not a normal reproducible run. Record the first divergence and minimal inputs.

Designer → Administration → Event log: select the short experiment interval and event filters. Only configured events appear. A missing entry does not prove no operation happened; correlate time/module/reference with an independent reread.

Technical messages can include paths, queries and personal data. Keep raw logs private; share classifications and synthetic examples. Avoid hiding useful causes behind “try later,”but do not publish indiscriminately. Define log retention separately.

Open the document object module, break on range validation and start debugging with F5. Perform the own invalid write; inspect duration and refusal, then continue. Remove breakpoints afterwards and do not edit values during the accepted run.

Preserve failing case, hypothesis, attempt, outcome and cause. After fixing, repeat original and neighboring cases, including failure/preservation. If the issue disappears only under a debugger, investigate ordering/timing. Retain failed experiments to document boundaries and prevent repeating false paths.

Use the defect cycle: reproduce, hypothesize range validation, observe 1441/refusal, correct input 45, reread 45 and regress the earlier 30/rejection. Retain both outcomes. Keep user messages clear and technical details in the safe own protocol.
